verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev is a code-first workflow platform. Its tasks are "plain async/await functions with no workflow DSL", and nothing in the evidence shows an ops-facing builder for conditional branches, filters, or parallel paths that merge. triggerAndWait and run-status filtering in the dashboard are developer building blocks and an adjacent feature, so they earn no credit toward this story.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can branch a workflow with conditions, filters, and parallel paths that merge back together
